topic: Your alternator can overcharge a battery — and it looks nothing like a dead one
negativePromptStanding: faces, hands, human figures, on-screen text, logos, watermarks, subtitles

beats.narration: Your headlights look brighter than usual at night. That's not always a good sign.
beats.visualPrompt: Night exterior shot: a car's headlights glowing unusually bright/white against a dark driveway or street, static-mounted camera, shallow depth of field.

beats.narration: Dash lights flicker or seem too bright. The battery case looks a little swollen.
beats.visualPrompt: Close-up on a dashboard cluster with lighting flickering slightly; cut to a macro shot of a car battery case with a visibly bulged/rounded top (not flat), dim garage lighting.

beats.narration: One clue: the alternator can overcharge the battery — pushing more voltage than it should.
beats.visualPrompt: Macro/cutaway shot: an alternator on a workbench or still mounted in an engine bay, slow push-in, no hands or tools visible in frame.

beats.narration: That extra voltage can cook a battery from the inside — long before it ever looks dead.
beats.visualPrompt: Close-up on a multimeter display showing a voltage reading, needle/digits trending above a normal reference band, screen glow in a dim shop bay, meter mounted/clipped in frame (no hand holding it).

beats.narration: Don't guess at the voltage. A quick test can show what the charging system is actually doing.
beats.visualPrompt: Multimeter probes resting clipped onto battery terminals under the hood, cable leads visible, shop bay softly blurred in the background.

beats.narration: Worth checking before it costs you a battery. Stop by and we'll take a look. Nick's Tire & Auto.
beats.visualPrompt: Branded end-card plate: Nick's Tire & Auto shop bay wide shot, warm daylight, static hold. Logo and CTA text composited in post, never AI-generated.

postingSpecs.feedCaption: Headlights looking brighter than usual at night? One clue mechanics check: an alternator that's overcharging the battery — it can cook a battery long before it ever looks dead. Don't guess at the voltage. Stop by and we'll take a look.
